result:
**I'd make curiosity contagious.**

Not forced, not mandated by some top-down "be smarter" program—just a world where the default human setting is *wonder* instead of certainty. Where people get the same dopamine hit from admitting "I don't know" and chasing the answer as they currently get from being right on the internet.

Everything else cascades from that:

- Tribalism weakens when you're more excited about what's true than what feels good to your group.
- Most scams (ideological, financial, spiritual) stop working when people instinctively ask better questions.
- We'd waste less time on performative outrage and more on building weird, beautiful, useful things.

The universe is already unspeakably strange and magnificent. We just mostly walk around with our eyes half-closed, shouting at each other. I'd flip the default from "comfortable delusion" to "delighted curiosity."

Everything good follows from there.
